turns.question: Where is application-level route handling wired up, and is the router itself implemented inside this repository?
turns.text:
I'll explore the express repo structure and find route-handling wiring, then confirm whether the router is implemented in this repo.This confirms it clearly. Here's the answer:

## Where application-level route handling is wired up

**`lib/application.js`** — this is where `app.use()`, `app.route()`, `app.get/post/...` (via the `methods.forEach` loop), `app.all()`, and `app.param()` are all defined. Every one of these is a thin proxy that delegates to a `Router` instance:

- `app.init()` (line ~53) lazily creates `this.router = new Router({ caseSensitive, strict })`
- `app.handle()` calls `this.router.handle(req, res, done)` to dispatch each request
- `app.use()` calls `router.use(path, fn)`
- `app.route()` calls `this.router.route(path)`
- `app.param()` calls `this.router.param(name, fn)`
- the per-HTTP-method shortcuts (`app.get`, `app.post`, etc.) call `this.route(path)[method](...)`

**`lib/express.js`** wires the app factory: `createApplication()` mixes `application.js`'s prototype onto the app function, and also re-exports `exports.Router = Router` and `exports.Route = Router.Route` for public use (e.g. `express.Router()`).

## Is the router implemented in this repo?

**No.** Both `lib/application.js` and `lib/express.js` do `var Router = require('router');` — this is the external npm package **`router`**, listed in `package.json` dependencies as `"router": "^2.2.0"`, not a local file. There is no `lib/router/` directory in this repository (confirmed via `ghx tree` — `lib/` only contains `application.js`, `express.js`, `request.js`, `response.js`, `utils.js`, `view.js`).

This is a structural change from Express 4.x, where routing logic (`lib/router/index.js`, `layer.js`, `route.js`) lived inside the express repo itself. In this version (Express 5.2.1), that logic has been extracted into the standalone [`router`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/router) package (also maintained under the expressjs org), and `express` itself is just the application/middleware layer built on top of it.

**Not verified:** I did not fetch the `router` npm package's own source (it's a separate repository, `expressjs/router`) to inspect its internal implementation — that would require a separate `ghx explore expressjs/router` call, which I didn't do since the question only asked whether the router lives *inside this repo*.
